title: Write a Grafana Dashboard as Code: Rate, Errors, Duration
intro: A dashboard built by clicking lives in one Grafana and has no history. As a JSON file in Git it can be reviewed, reused for every service, and restored. Write the smallest useful service dashboard: request rate, error ratio, and p99 latency, with a variable for the namespace. Grafana's dashboard format is JSON.

steps.prompt:
Write checkout-dashboard.json, a JSON object with:

- "title": "Checkout Service", "uid": "checkout-overview", "refresh": "30s"
- "time": {"from": "now-6h", "to": "now"}
- "templating": {"list": [ one variable ]} where the variable has "name": "namespace", "type": "query", and
  "query": "label_values(http_requests_total, namespace)"
- "panels": three panels, each with "type": "timeseries", a "title", a "targets" list holding one object with an "expr",
  and "fieldConfig": {"defaults": {"unit": ...}}:

  1. "Request rate", unit "reqps":
     sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="checkout",namespace="$namespace"}[5m]))
  2. "Error ratio", unit "percentunit":
     sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="checkout",namespace="$namespace",status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="checkout",namespace="$namespace"}[5m]))
  3. "p99 latency", unit "s":
     histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service="checkout",namespace="$namespace"}[5m])))

Inside JSON strings, escape the inner double quotes as \".
steps.hint:
Overall shape:
{
  "title": "Checkout Service",
  "uid": "checkout-overview",
  "refresh": "30s",
  "time": {"from": "now-6h", "to": "now"},
  "templating": {"list": [{"name": "namespace", "type": "query", "query": "label_values(http_requests_total, namespace)"}]},
  "panels": [
    {"title": "Request rate", "type": "timeseries",
     "targets": [{"expr": "sum(rate(http_requests_total{service=\"checkout\",namespace=\"$namespace\"}[5m]))"}],
     "fieldConfig": {"defaults": {"unit": "reqps"}}},
    ...
  ]
}
No trailing commas: JSON doesn't allow them.
steps.fake_output:
(valid JSON)

$ curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $GRAFANA_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d "{\"dashboard\": $(cat checkout-dashboard.json), \"overwrite\": true}" $GRAFANA_URL/api/dashboards/db
{"status":"success","uid":"checkout-overview","version":1}
steps.explanation: Three panels that answer 'how much traffic, how many errors, how slow' for one service, in any namespace.
steps.why: Rate, errors, and duration (RED) are the three graphs every request-serving service needs, and they come first on a dashboard because they're what users experience. Details that matter. The fixed uid gives the dashboard a stable URL and lets the same file update it in place instead of creating copies. The variable turns one dashboard into one per namespace; a second variable for the service would make it a template for every service. The error panel is a ratio, not a count, so it means the same thing at 3 a.m. and at peak. The latency panel is a percentile from a histogram, grouped 'by (le)' (leaving that out is the bug in monitoring-incident-003), and never an average, which hides the slow requests. Units make the axes readable: 'percentunit' shows 0.05 as 5%. Load the file with Grafana's provisioning or the API from a pipeline, and turn off editing in the UI so the file stays the truth.
